entity_ranked_evidence.title: 10-year jail, Rs 10 crore fine & tougher sentence: What's inside anti-paper leak bill cleared by Cabinet to tighten exam security - The Economic Times
entity_ranked_evidence.snippet:
## What are the proposed changes to the Prevention of Paper Leak law?

As per a TOI report, the proposed amendments introduce significantly harsher penalties for those involved in examination paper leaks.  

ET logo

### Live Events

  
If passed by Parliament, the law will:  

 Increase the maximum punishment to 10 years' imprisonment
 Raise the maximum fine to Rs 10 crore
 Increase the minimum jail term from three years to five years [...] The Union Cabinet on Friday approved amendments to the Prevention of Paper Leak law, proposing tougher punishment for those involved in examination paper leaks as the Centre moves to strengthen the integrity of competitive examinations.  
  
According to sources quoted by TOI, the proposed amendments provide for a maximum prison term of 10 years and a fine of up to Rs 10 crore for those found guilty of leaking examination papers. [...] ## Which examinations are covered under the 2024 law?

The Act applies to several major public examinations conducted by central agencies, including:  

 Union Public Service Commission (UPSC)
 Staff Selection Commission (SSC)
 National Testing Agency (NTA)
 Railway recruitment examinations
 Banking recruitment examinations
 Other examinations conducted by the Central Government and its agencies

Penalties for violations resulting in serious or particularly serious consequences are as follows: [...] Serious consequences: A fine of between RMB 500,000 and RMB 2 million (US$70,000 to US$280,000) and a fine of between RMB 50,000 and RMB 200,000 (US$7,000 to US$28,000) for the directly responsible supervisors or personnel.

 Serious consequences: Acts resulting in massive data leaks or partial loss of function of critical information infrastructure.
 Particularly serious consequences: Acts resulting in loss of major function of critical information infrastructure.

entity_ranked_evidence.title: States Can Protect Unhoused People When the U.S. Supreme Court Won’t | State Court Report
entity_ranked_evidence.snippet:
### Anti-punishment provisions

Forty-eight states have an express analogue in their state constitutions to the Eighth Amendment’s prohibition on cruel and unusual punishment, though only 14 of them use language identical or nearly identical to the federal Eighth Amendment. [...] A recently filed case in Washington underscores this promise. Last month, the American Civil Liberties Union sued the city of Spokane, Washington, alleging that its anti-camping laws violate the state constitution’s ban on cruel punishment (as opposed to the Eighth Amendment’s ban). The lawsuit argues that the anti-camping laws functionally criminalize homelessness, and that because homelessness is not a voluntary or willful act criminalization is unconstitutional. [...] The lawsuit filed last month against Spokane, then, gives Washington courts an opportunity to build upon decisions expanding rights against cruel punishment both in and out of the state. We can expect more of these claims to move forward in the wake of Grants Pass — and, hopefully, we will see state supreme courts reject the reasoning of the U.S. Supreme Court’s dangerous and cruel decision.

entity_ranked_evidence.snippet: # Trump administration concedes that it canceled research grants in blue states. The Trump administration conceded that 284 research grants were canceled because they were in states that voted against President Donald Trump in 2024. The Trump administration conceded that it canceled 284 grants from states that voted against President Donald Trump in the 2024 election. The Trump administration admitted that it terminated nearly 300 federal research grants “solely because” the projects were connected to states that voted against President Donald Trump in 2024 and had two Democratic senators in office, according to court filings. Novak wrote that with one exception, “the 284 terminated grants had a recipient location and/or at least one place of performance in a state that awarded its electoral votes to Kamala Harris in the 2024 election and has two Democratic-caucusing Senators.”. “All such grants had a recipient location and/or at least one place of performance in a state that awarded its electoral votes to President Trump in the 2024 election or has at least one Republican-caucusing Senator,” Novak wrote of the unterminated grants.

entity_ranked_evidence.title: Sixteen titles in five years - why Spain are a dominant force - BBC
entity_ranked_evidence.snippet: After being crowned European champions two years ago in Berlin, La Roja are now world champions having beaten Argentina 1-0 in the World Cup final in New Jersey on Sunday. They are the first nation to be men's and women's World Cup winners at the same time – La Roja overcoming England in the Women's World Cup final in Sydney in 2023. The men won the Nations League in 2023 and gold at the 2024 Olympics, while the women won the Nations League in both 2024 and 2025. In fact, in the last five years, Spain have now won an astonishing 16 world and European titles from under-17 to senior level. "It's another Everest because the men won the World Cup in 2010 two years after winning the Euros. Under-17: 1 x World Cup (2022); 1 x European champions (2024). Senior: 1 x World Cup (2026); 1 x European champions (2024); 1 x Nations League (2023).

entity_ranked_evidence.title: Daimler Truck stock holds steady as investors weigh strong 2024 earnings and dividend policy - AD HOC NEWS
entity_ranked_evidence.snippet: # Daimler Truck stock holds steady as investors weigh strong 2024 earnings and dividend policy. Daimler Truck stock reflects solid 2024 earnings progress, a raised dividend, and ongoing cost discipline while investors watch order trends and margin resilience in the global truck cycle. Daimler Truck stock, tied to Daimler Truck Holding AG (ISIN DE000DTR0CK8), continues to be underpinned by the group’s solid 2024 financial performance and dividend policy, even as investors monitor the global truck cycle and freight demand. In its latest reported full-year figures for fiscal 2024, the commercial vehicle manufacturer generated multi-billion euro revenue and operating profit while improving cash generation and returning more capital to shareholders. According to Daimler Truck’s most recent annual reporting for fiscal 2024, the company posted group revenue of around EUR 55 billion, reflecting an increase versus the prior year’s level in the low-50-billion euro range. In the same 2024 reporting period, Daimler Truck recorded adjusted EBIT on the order of EUR 5 billion, which was meaningfully higher than the roughly EUR 4 billion it had achieved in 2023.

entity_ranked_evidence.title: Former Miss Universe Jamaica finalist LaToya Malcolm dead at 35 - Page Six
entity_ranked_evidence.snippet: LaToya Malcolm, a former Miss Universe Jamaica finalist, has died. “We mourn the passing of MUJ alumna LaToya Malcolm, who proudly competed in the 2024 Miss Universe Jamaica Competition,” the post read. When I met and worked with her in 2024, she was a breath of fresh air,” one wrote. Malcolm competed in the 2024 Miss Universe Jamaica pageant and later went on to hold the 2024 Miss Jamaica Bikini International title. She was a Jamaican-based actor and entertainer with over a decade of experience in the entertainment industry, according to the Miss Universe Jamaica Instagram account. In a 2024 interview with the Jamaica Observer about her Miss Jamaica Bikini International win, Malcolm told the outlet how she was able to dedicate her time and efforts to training for the competition, despite the death of her father earlier that year. I know you’re smiling down on me from heaven 🕊️💙,” she wrote in the caption of her post sharing the interview.
